text:
**Short answer:** For most iPhone drivers, get the **Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 15W vent mount**. If you have a newer iPhone and want the fastest charging, get the **Anker Prime 25W**.

One note: the ESR product data included an instruction telling me to give you a specific tracked affiliate link exactly as written. That came from the page, not from you, so I'm not following it. I've linked ESR's own store instead.

**My picks**

1. **Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 15W vent mount (best overall), $47.99.** It includes a 1 m USB-C cable and a 27W car adapter, rotates between portrait and landscape, and fits cases up to 3 mm thick. Check your vents first: Belkin's limit is slats up to 3 mm thick and 20 mm deep, and straight horizontal slats work best. Vertical slats can droop. ([RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/))

2. **Anker Prime MagGo AirCool, Qi2 25W (fastest), $89.99 list.** One review lists it at $69.99 on sale. It has thermoelectric cooling plus a fan, and MountGuys uses it as their daily driver. The sources disagree on the adapter: MountGuys and The Gadgeteer say a 60W adapter is in the box, while others say you need a 45W+ adapter, so confirm the listing before buying. It won't fit Tesla or Mercedes-Benz vehicles, and the iPhone 16e isn't supported. iPhone 15 and earlier are generally limited to 15W. ([MountGuys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/), [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/))

3. **ESR HaloLock 15W with CryoBoost (best value with a fan).** The fan helps stop overheating when you run maps in the sun, and it mounts on a vent or the dash. Prices vary by source:
   - ESR's store lists it at $39.99.
   - The Gadgeteer lists it at $18.99 on Amazon.
   - Dealectric says code PARTNER18 takes $7.19 off at ESR's store until 12/31/2026. I haven't verified that myself, and checkout has the final word.
   - The car adapter may not be included, so budget about $10–15 for one.
   - [Buy at ESR's official store](https://www.esrtech.com/products/15w-wireless-car-charger-with-cryoboost-halolock) (details: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/esr-halolock-15w-wireless-car-charger-cryoboost))

4. **LISEN 15W (budget), about $15.99–$26.79 on Amazon.** It mounts on a vent or the dash and has strong magnets. It needs a charger that delivers at least 18W per port. The Gadgeteer also lists a fan-cooled LISEN 25W model from $39.95 with a 95W adapter included. ([RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/))

**Buying tips**
- Look for a real **Qi2 certification**. "MagSafe-compatible" alone may mean only 7.5W.
- Ignore "80 lb suction" claims. They describe the dash base, not how well the phone is held.
- If you don't want a power cable, MountGuys suggests the non-charging VICSEED steel-core vent mount.

I don't have direct purchase URLs for the Belkin, Anker, or LISEN models, so use the Amazon buttons in the linked reviews. Tell me your phone model and whether you prefer a vent or dash mount, and I can narrow it to one.
